title: Strong monoidal functors preserve ring objects
statement:
Let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a lax monoidal functor between monoidal categories, with
structure maps $\mu^F_{X,Y}\colon FX\otimes FY\to F(X\otimes Y)$, natural in $X,Y$, and
$\varepsilon^F\colon\mathbf 1\to F\mathbf 1$, satisfying the usual associativity and unit
coherences. (A strong monoidal functor is the case where these are isomorphisms.) For a ring object
$(R,\mu,\eta)$ of $\mathcal C$ ([det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]) put
$$
\mu_{FR}:=F(\mu)\circ\mu^F_{R,R}\colon FR\otimes FR\to FR,\qquad \eta_{FR}:=F(\eta)\circ\varepsilon^F\colon\mathbf 1\to FR .
$$
Then:

1. $(FR,\mu_{FR},\eta_{FR})$ is a ring object of $\mathcal D$, and for a morphism $f$ of ring
   objects, $Ff$ is a morphism of ring objects; this defines a functor
   $\mathrm{Mon}(F)\colon\mathrm{Mon}(\mathcal C)\to\mathrm{Mon}(\mathcal D)$ over $F$;
2. if $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ are braided and $F$ is braided, i.e.
   $F(\beta_{X,Y})\circ\mu^F_{X,Y}=\mu^F_{Y,X}\circ\beta_{FX,FY}$, then $FR$ is commutative whenever
   $R$ is;
3. a monoidal natural transformation $\tau\colon F\Rightarrow F'$ between lax monoidal functors has
   components $\tau_R\colon FR\to F'R$ that are morphisms of ring objects; in particular a monoidal
   natural isomorphism gives isomorphic ring objects.

mathlib_match.how: Exact, one declaration per clause, with the stipulated operation formulas definitionally equal. Clause 1: CategoryTheory.Functor.mapMon at Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mon.lean:867–869 sends a bundled monoid A to F.obj A.X and a morphism f to F.map f.hom. Its structure is CategoryTheory.Functor.monObjObj at Mon.lean:827–836, with one := ε F ≫ F.map η and mul := LaxMonoidal.μ F X X ≫ F.map μ; CategoryTheory.Functor.map.instIsMonHom at Mon.lean:850–852 proves preservation of morphisms. Clause 2: CategoryTheory.Functor.isCommMonObj_obj at Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/CommMon_.lean:157–159, or equivalently CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCommMon at CommMon_.lean:169–176, requires only F.LaxBraided and braided source and target categories. Clause 3: CategoryTheory.Functor.mapMonNatTrans at Mon.lean:909–910 has component .mk' (τ.app A.X), and CategoryTheory.Functor.mapMonNatIso at Mon.lean:917–918 gives the claimed monoid isomorphism for a monoidal natural isomorphism. These require only lax monoidal F,F' and NatTrans.IsMonoidal τ. Ring objects here mean MonObj (Mon.lean:73–84), exactly the cited definition det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid, and not cartesian RingObj. LaxBraided is exactly the displayed braided equation (Braided/Basic.lean:386–388); NatTrans.IsMonoidal is exactly compatibility with ε and μ (NaturalTransformation.lean:46–48). Read Mon.lean:815–918 and CommMon_.lean:146–176; no added additivity, symmetry, closedness, or invertibility assumptions. Lean's ≫ is diagrammatic composition, so the formulas agree with the item's right-to-left composition. Taking the named constructions/components is a one-line application for each clause.
